title: Lost sleep adds up, and NHLBI says a nap does not repay the whole debt
summary: NHLBI calls the total sleep lost a sleep debt, and gives two lost hours a night as fourteen hours after a week.
body: The sleep-deprivation page says that if a person regularly loses sleep, or chooses to sleep less than needed, the loss adds up. It calls that total a sleep debt. Its example is that losing 2 hours each night leaves a debt of 14 hours after a week. Naps, it says, may give a short-term boost in alertness and performance, but napping does not supply all the other benefits of nighttime sleep, so a person cannot really make up for lost sleep that way. The arithmetic is the page's illustration. It is not a score for a child.

sources.title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency: How Much Sleep Is Enough
sources.author: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Supports the adult row and the sleep-debt example. Page last updated 24 March 2022.
